title: Majestic: Mate Before the Queen Can Help
summary: A new queen cannot rescue a trapped king when the other side can deliver an immediate pawn mate.

nodes.question: Should White race the pawn or move the king?
nodes.explanation: After ...g2, White has Ke7/f5/h6 against Kg8/Rh8/g2/h7. Black’s own king and pawn block the rook; White must use the remaining tempo.

branches.title: Promote the threat, not the pawn
commentary: After ...g2, White has Ke7/f5/h6 against Kg8/Rh8/g2/h7. Black’s own king and pawn block the rook; White must use the remaining tempo.
f6 threatens f7 mate. White’s h6 pawn and king cover the exits around Kg8.
g1=Q promotes, but the queen cannot interrupt the immediate mate or free Rh8 in time.
f7# is mate. The pawn checks g8; Ke7 covers f8/f7, h6 covers g7, and Black’s own Rh8/h7 occupy the other escape squares.
branches.explanation: f7# is mate. The pawn checks g8; Ke7 covers f8/f7, h6 covers g7, and Black’s own Rh8/h7 occupy the other escape squares.

branches.title: Independent knight underpromotion cannot save Black
commentary: After ...g2, White has Ke7/f5/h6 against Kg8/Rh8/g2/h7. Black’s own king and pawn block the rook; White must use the remaining tempo.
g1=N is an independently checked underpromotion defense. The knight on g1 cannot stop f7.
f7# is still actual mate. Underpromotion does not change the trapped king’s flight squares.

branches.explanation: f7# is still actual mate. Underpromotion does not change the trapped king’s flight squares.

branches.title: Independent king retreat wastes the tempo
commentary: After ...g2, White has Ke7/f5/h6 against Kg8/Rh8/g2/h7. Black’s own king and pawn block the rook; White must use the remaining tempo.
Kd6 spends the essential tempo away from the f-pawn and gives up the forced win. The resulting exact outcome is checked rather than inferred from Black’s material advantage.

exercises.prompt: Why does Black’s extra queen fail to matter?
exercises.answer: White does not need to promote. The next pawn move is mate, and Black’s own pieces occupy its king’s remaining escape squares.

startContext: Only the final seven-piece pawn-race diagram after ...g2 at 147s is verified here. The earlier larger rook-skewer, h6 restraint and Ke7 rook sacrifice remain source context. Queen promotion and f7 mate are illustrated; knight underpromotion and the king retreat are independent comparisons.
